---
title: "M&Ms Analysis"
format: html
---

Load in Data:

```{r}
df_url="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jmayberr/math133-stat-learning-fall2026/refs/heads/main/Datasets/MandMs.csv"
skittles=read.csv(df_url)
head(skittles)
```

```{r}
totals=colSums(skittles[,2:6])
barplot(totals)
```

Expected Totals

```{r}
n=sum(totals)
expected=rep(n/5,5)
expected
totals
```

Model Evaluation

```{r}
rmse_observed=sqrt(mean((totals-expected)^2))
rmse_observed
```

Simulating machines

```{r}
colors=c("red","orange","yellow","green","purple")
s=sample(colors,n,replace=TRUE)
table(s)
rmse_machine=sqrt(mean((table(s)-expected)^2))
rmse_machine
```

```{r}
rmse=function(s){
  sqrt(mean((table(s)-expected)^2))
}

rmse_machines=replicate(10000,
                        rmse(sample(colors,n,replace=TRUE))
                        )

```

```{r}
hist(rmse_machines)
abline(v=rmse_observed,col="darkred")
```

```{r}
sum(rmse_machines>=rmse_observed)/10000 # p-value
```

$\chi^2$ Goodness of Fit Test

Uses theoretical reference distribution: Chi-square with $k-1$ degrees of freedom where $k$ = number of categories (5 for skittles).

```{r}
chi=sum((totals-expected)^2/expected)
chi
```

```{r}
1-pchisq(chi,4) #Prob that a chi-square with 4 df > chi
```
